newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called 50 cts up, Brent 5-10 cts firme.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called 50 cts up, Brent 5-10 cts firme.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were called to open slightly higher on Wednesday on the back of neutral to bullish API data and unseasonably cool temperatures in Northwest Europe, brokers said.
May gas oil was expected to open around 50 cents up on the Tuesday close of $166.50 a tonne. June Brent was seen opening up some five to 10 cents up after closing at $18.07 a barrel.
"We had a look at the down side yesterday and failed. I think we're looking for a slight move up," said one dealer.

Brokers said that record U.S. gasoline demand implied by American Petroleum Institute (API) stocks data for last week was the main market driver, although some were sceptical that the data was accurate.
The API report showed "implied demand" for gasoline running at 8.76 million barrels a day last week in the run-up to the peak summer driving season.
"It seems a little bit unbelievable, but your gut reaction is to go along with it until we get confirmation," a dealer said.
Stocks data from the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) were expected at 1300 GMT.
API data showed a crude draw of 1.9 million barrels excluding the PADD 5 west coast region, which operates more or less independently from the rest of the country.
Nationally, stocks rose 1.02 million barrels, against expectations of a two million barrel build.
But distillate stocks defied expectations of a draw due to cold weather in the Northeast market, and stocks rose by 2.7 million barrels.
But cooler temperatures in Northwest Europe were expected to lend support to gas oil nevertheless.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) said that temperatures in the region were expected to hold below seasonal norms for the next two days.
